intentions.title: Ship a provider-neutral cloud-provisioning seam so Hetzner and Azure (and future clouds) plug in as implementations, never forks
intentions.evidence: provider.go defines a deliberately narrow CloudProvider interface (Create/IP/Delete/List) plus optional capability interfaces (Cataloger, Archiver, Resurrector, Decommissioner, Adopter, Auditor, Pauser, ServerLabeler/LabelLister/ServerLabelRemover); registry.go's ProviderFor resolves a slug to a factory so 'a new provider lands as a Register call, not a new switch arm'; azure/provider.go and fake.go both satisfy the same seam.

intentions.title: Turn go-live provisioning into an instant, always-warm operation via a self-refilling warm host pool instead of create-on-demand
intentions.evidence: warmpool.go: Pool.pop() returns a ready host AND triggers a replacement create (refill) in one call; WarmPool.Provision chains assign→secrets→dns→caddy→secrets-install→migrate→admin-token→health→register, described as 'local Barkpark → live server in seconds is a warm-pool move, not a create-on-demand one'.

intentions.title: Make the go-live chain fail closed: no server is ever registered as live unless the post-deploy health gate passes
intentions.evidence: warmpool.go doc comment: 'The chain FAILS CLOSED: if the health gate does not pass, Provision returns an error and does NOT register the server or mark it ready'; pollHealth bounds retries via healthPollDeadline/healthPollInterval and only succeeds on report.OK.

intentions.title: Guarantee every provisioned tenant gets fully independent cryptographic identity — no shared secrets across instances
intentions.evidence: warmpool.go Secrets struct (SecretKeyBase, Kek, CloakKey, PreviewJWTSecret) each drawn from an INDEPENDENT crypto/rand call in defaultSecretGen; secretsInstallStep documents that the baked warm image bakes a SHARED key across tenants and this step exists precisely to replace it per-instance before migrate runs (runtime.exs requires BARKPARK_KEK).

intentions.title: Prevent secret leakage through provisioning failures — every step's captured output is scrubbed before it can reach logs, error columns, or worker stderr
intentions.evidence: warmpool.go: CaddyStep.Redact (literal substrings) + RedactEnvSecrets (pattern-based scrubEnvSecrets for SECRET_KEY_BASE/BARKPARK_KEK/BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY/PREVIEW_JWT_SECRET/DATABASE_URL and ecto/postgres userinfo) funnel through scrubStepOutput before any fmt.Errorf; adminTokenStep, agentInstallStep, secretsInstallStep all set Redact/RedactEnvSecrets; validateAdminToken/validateSecretValue/validateAgentURL guard against shell-injection before interpolation.

intentions.title: Build a provider-portable disaster-recovery format (bp-bundle-v1) so an instance archived on one cloud can be resurrected on a different one
intentions.evidence: bundle.go: WriteBundle streams db.dump, media.tar.gz, AES-256-GCM sealed secrets.enc, then manifest.json LAST as a completeness fence (torn uploads are invisible to readers); IdentitySecretKeys/SelectIdentitySecrets carry the identity secrets needed to decrypt the Cloak-encrypted DB after cross-provider restore; contrasted explicitly against the project-bound Hetzner snapshot path.

intentions.title: Make provider capability gaps honest and renderable rather than silently faked — a provider only claims what it actually implements
intentions.evidence: provider.go Capabilities struct + DetectCapabilities: lifecycle facets (Archive/Resurrect/Decommission/Adopt/Audit) are independent bools, two-source detected (interface satisfaction OR RegisterLifecycleVerbs registration); registry.go's committed providers_capabilities.json fixture is the canonical cross-surface contract with a parity test failing on drift; comments state Azure has 'honest decommission + audit but no snapshot-based archive/resurrect'.

intentions.title: Keep every external dependency (cloud API, DNS API, SSH, object storage) behind an injectable interface so the whole provisioning chain is testable at zero spend
intentions.evidence: fake.go's FakeProvider/FakeBundleStore, dns.go's FakeDNS, and warmpool.go's injected StepRunner/HealthChecker/RegistryClient/SecretGen seams all mirror real production paths (HcloudProvider, HetznerDNS, SSHStepRunner) with deterministic in-memory behavior; FakeProvider is marked as honoring every optional capability so real providers are 'verified for equivalence against this behaviour'.

intentions.title: Give the fleet resilience against sold-out server types/regions via an automatic fallback ladder
intentions.evidence: provider.go's HetznerCandidates + CreateWithFallback walk an ordered ladder of type/location alternatives and aggregate all failures into one legible error; used by both SeedPool and Pool.pop's refill so ARM (cax) stockouts don't block go-lives.

intentions.title: Never strand a paid box: recover from create/delete failures automatically via orphan labeling and sweep
intentions.evidence: provider.go: ManagedLabelKey/OrphanedLabelKey/FQDNLabelKey/WarmLabelKey scheme; HcloudProvider.Create deletes a just-created server if IP read-back fails ('so a failed IP read-back never leaks a paid box'); ListByLabel/LabelServer are the safe inputs SweepOrphans relies on to find and clean up boxes truly meant to be gone.
